sentences.text: AUGUST 19, 2023 Anticipatory Bail Application No. 700 OF 2023

Between:
Rahul Dobhal. ............Applicant.
And State of Uttarakhand. .......Respondent.
Counsel for the applicant: Mr. Akshay Pradhan, learned counsel  for the applicant.
Counsel for the respondents: Mr. V.S. Rathore, learned A.G.A. for  the State.

Upon hearing the learned Counsel, the Court made the following Order:
(per Sri Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
1.

This is an application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking anticipatory bail in respect of FIR No. 0246 of 2023 for the offences cognizable under Sections 120-B, 420, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC, registered at P.S. - Kotwali, District - Dehradun.
2. As per the FIR lodged on 25.06.2023 by one Ashwini Kumar S/o Late Nagendra Dutt, ten persons and the officers of the Revenue Department are implicated.

As per the allegations, the father of the complainant sold two parcels of land to Golden Forest and Multiple Associates in 1995 and 2001 and by committing forgery, the names were mutated in the year 2007 in the revenue records in the name of Multiple Associates and, subsequently, the land was sold by Multiple Associates to various individuals including one firm namely M/s Sunset Wildwell.

3. Counsel for the applicant submits that the present applicant Rahul Dobhal is a bonafide purchaser, who purchased a piece of land from M/s Sunset Wildwell by way of a registered sale deed dated 01.10.2018 with a consideration of Rs. 70 lakhs.
(Copy of the sale deed is annexed as Annexure No. 2 to the petition).

1 4.

Counsel for the applicant further submits that Original Suit No. 9 of 2021 was also preferred by the father of the complainant Nagendra Dutt in the Court of learned Civil Judge (J.D.), Dehradun,
which is still pending, wherein, against the seller M/s Sunset Wildwell as well as present applicant also implicated as defendant no. 3.
In the said suit, the sale deed dated 03.05.2007, sale deed dated 01.10.2018 and subsequent sale deed were sought to be declared as null and void.
Though, the suit was filed in the year 2021, but with an ulterior purpose the FIR has been lodged on 25.06.2023.

The petitioner submits that another co-accused namely Sanjay Ghai in respect of the same FIR No. 0246 of 2023 has been granted the interim protection by Coordinate Bench of this Court by an order dated 18.07.2023 in ABA No. 572 of 2023.
5. Counsel for the applicant submits that he purchased the land from M/s Sunset Wildwell on 01.10.2018 and M/s Sunset Wildwell purchased the said land from Sanjay Ghai in the year 2007.
Sanjay Ghai purchased this property from the father of the complainant in the year 1995.
Counsel for the petitioner further submits that there is immediate threat of arrest to the present applicant.

Learned counsel submits that the allegations are civil in nature and that is the reason that the civil suit was filed by the father of the applicant.
6.

On the other side, the State Counsel has raised a serious objection that by procuring the forged document the mutations were carried out in connivance of the officers of the Revenue Department;
however, he sought three weeks' time to file counter affidavit for the purpose of filing objection in respect of anticipatory bail.

7. Let the objection be filed within a period of three weeks.
8.

List this matter on 13.09.2023.
9.

Having considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merit of this case, this Court directs that in event of arrest of the present applicant, he shall be released on interim anticipatory bail on furnishing a personal bond by him to the satisfaction of the arresting officer subject to the following conditions:
(i) The applicant shall not approach, in any manner, whatsoever, the victims or any other witnesses in the case.
(ii) He shall cooperate with the investigation.
He shall not leave the country without permission of the concerned court.
(iii) He shall deposit the passport, if any, with the Investigating Officer within a week.
The passport may only be returned by the order of the Court concerned.
In case the applicant does not have the passport, he shall give an undertaking in respect of the aforesaid conditions before the Investigating Officer.

__________________ RAKESH THAPLIYAL, J.
